Describe a change between two periods in plain English

Source: R/describe-change.R
describe_change.Rd

Turns the two-row table from compare_periods() into one sentence a non-specialist can read, such as "In Perth, days at or above 35 degrees C have become more common: ...". The sentence states the direction, both averages, the size of the change and, when it is meaningful, the ratio. It also says so when a period has no usable seasons, instead of reporting a misleading number.

Usage

describe_change(
  comparison,
  what = "very hot days",
  place = NULL,
  tolerance = 0.5,
  digits = 1
)

Arguments

comparison

A tibble returned by compare_periods().

what

A plural noun phrase for what was counted, for example "days at or above 35 degrees C" or "frosty nights".

place

Optional place name to start the sentence with.

tolerance

Differences smaller than this (in days per season) are described as "about the same". Defaults to 0.5.

digits

Decimal places for the averages. Defaults to 1.

Value

A single character string.

Examples

perth <- count_hot_days(fire_season_temps, "Perth")
compare_periods(perth) |>
  describe_change(what = "days at or above 35 degrees C", place = "Perth")
#> [1] "In Perth, days at or above 35 degrees C have become more common: recent seasons (1989–2018) averaged 26.0 per season, compared with 17.0 in 1910–1939, an increase of 9.0 per season (1.5 times the early average)."

# When a period has no data, the sentence says so
count_hot_days(fire_season_temps, "Brisbane") |>
  compare_periods() |>
  describe_change(what = "very hot days", place = "Brisbane")
#> [1] "In Brisbane, the early period (1910–1939) has no complete seasons, so no change can be stated."
